title: Access Curator: Terraform module to produce minimal IAM roles for Private/VPC deploys
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Goal: Build a reusable Terraform module (access-curator) that generates least-privilege IAM roles/policies for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments. The module must be opinionated but extensible: accept a small service descriptor (permissions intent + resource scopes), output role and policy artifacts, attach cross-account trust where required, and emit policy metadata for drift detection and audit. This is not just a policy template library — it should include validation, automated policy slimming heuristics, and CI-friendly tests so platform engineers can safely onboard new services without hand-writing policies.
acceptance_criteria:
- Module produces deterministic policy JSON given the same descriptor inputs.
- Generated policies are scoped to resource ARNs and include IAM condition blocks for time-bound or session-tag constraints when requested.
- Terratest and unit mocks validate at least three common service patterns (API server, batch worker, infra-controller).
- TF module exposes a "role_catalog" output describing roles, allowed actions, and attached resources for Console and audit ingestion.
- CI pipeline runs tfsec/checkov and a policy-sim (aws iam simulate-principal-policy) step and fails on high-severity findings.
- Documented upgrade and migration plan for existing manual roles with a rollback path.
design_decisions:
- Use a compact service descriptor schema: name, env, resources, intents (read/write/admin), trust_accounts, session_tag_keys.
- Implement policy-slimming heuristics that remove broad "*" permissions, prefer action lists and service-specific prefixes, and recommend managed policy splits for reusable surfaces.
- Emit both IAM JSON and a normalized YAML metadata file for easier diffs in PRs and Console ingestion.
- Provide an optional OPA/Rego policy bundle to run in CI for custom organizational guardrails.
- Avoid runtime runtime runtime... (jk): module will not attempt runtime token rotation — that remains in KMS/HSM integration work.
